facts.raw_span: A 42-year-old man
underwent transthoracic echocardiography as part of a routine medical checkup
which revealed a left ventricular mass
He had no prior medical history
denied fever, weight loss, dyspnea, or other symptoms
his temperature was 36.5 °C
blood pressure 120/80 mm Hg
electrocardiogram showed normal sinus rhythm
A chest radiograph revealed no active lung lesions
Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a mobile, smooth, oval, pedunculated mass originating from the left ventricular lateral wall, measuring 1.34 × 1.9 cm
Contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography showed the mass attached to the interventricular septum with focal contrast enhancement
